label: Dijon Mustard
note: Claims dijon + spicy brown (both excluded by the yellow-mustard rule). Honey-dijon is routed to honey-mustard on purpose; dry ground/seed mustard spice excluded.

label: Honey Mustard
note: Requires both words together so plain honey (existing) and yellow mustard are unaffected. Honey-dijon claimed here. Snack/pretzel/nut forms excluded.

label: Miracle Whip (Salad Dressing Spread)
note: Bare 'salad dressing' deliberately NOT included (would grab pourable ranch/italian/caesar). Matches Miracle Whip + store-brand 'whipped dressing' spreads; real mayo (existing) excluded.

label: Caesar Dressing
note: Bottled prepared dressing only; caesar salad kits, croutons, and dry caesar mix packets excluded.

label: Blue Cheese Dressing
note: Requires 'dressing' so cheese-aisle blue cheese crumbles/wedges are excluded. A 'Dressing & Dip' bottle still matches; a purely refrigerated produce-case dip cannot be told apart by name, so it is left in.

label: Balsamic Vinegar
note: 'vinegar' is not a substring of 'vinaigrette', so balsamic vinaigrette dressing and balsamic glaze/reduction are excluded belt-and-suspenders. White/red-wine vinegar unaffected.

label: Rice Vinegar
note: Catches 'rice vinegar' and 'rice wine vinegar' (same product). Seasoned rice vinegar kept (per notes); mirin/cooking wine (near-neighbors on the shelf) excluded. Plain rice grain never matches (needs 'vinegar').

label: Red Wine Vinegar
note: Full phrase required, so WHITE wine vinegar and balsamic never match. Red-wine-vinegar dressings/vinaigrettes excluded.

label: Teriyaki Sauce / Marinade
note: Claims teriyaki sauce AND teriyaki marinade (same bottle). Soy sauce (existing) already excludes teriyaki, so no reverse collision. Frozen teriyaki meals/bowls, jerky, ramen/noodles, and dry seasoning excluded.

label: Steak Sauce (A.1. style)
note: Include 'steak sauce' (not bare 'steak', so raw steak never matches) plus A.1./Heinz 57 brands. Marinades (own item), steak seasoning/rub, and jerky excluded. Worcestershire/BBQ (existing) don't match these includes.

label: Cocktail Sauce
note: Seafood cocktail sauce (the ketchup/horseradish condiment). Excludes shrimp-cocktail party trays and drink 'cocktail mixers' (margarita/bloody mary/mocktail). Ketchup and tartar sauce don't match this phrase.

label: Tartar Sauce
note: Requires 'sauce' so the baking ingredient 'cream of tartar' never matches (also explicitly excluded). Mayo (existing) and cocktail sauce don't match this phrase.

label: Prepared Horseradish
note: Covers prepared horseradish + creamy horseradish sauce. Excludes wasabi (horseradish-based but distinct), horseradish mustard (a mustard), horseradish cheese spread, and fresh horseradish root.

label: Enchilada Sauce
note: Full phrase 'enchilada sauce' covers red and green canned sauce without grabbing frozen enchilada dinners/kits or enchilada seasoning mix. Taco sauce (candidate) and salsa/hot sauce (existing) don't match.

label: Taco Sauce
note: Include 'taco sauce' (not bare 'taco', so shells/kits/seasoning are avoided). Salsa (existing), enchilada sauce (candidate), and taco seasoning packets explicitly excluded.

label: Sloppy Joe Sauce (Manwich style)
note: Canned sloppy joe sauce. Excludes dry sloppy joe seasoning packets and frozen/ready sloppy joe sandwiches. BBQ/pasta sauce (existing) don't match.

label: Meat Marinade (bottled)
note: Catch-all bottled liquid marinade. Excludes items that own their board slot (teriyaki, italian dressing, BBQ) and dry marinade MIX packets/rubs. 'marinade' is not a substring of 'marinated', so marinated artichokes/olives are unaffected.

label: Pesto (jarred)
note: Jarred pesto sauce. Prepared pesto dishes (tortellini/ravioli/pizza/frozen) and pesto snack chips/crackers excluded. Refrigerated fresh pesto cannot be distinguished from shelf-stable by name, so it is left in.

label: Minced Garlic (jarred)
note: Wet jarred minced/chopped/crushed garlic in water or oil. Garlic powder, garlic salt, fresh bulbs, and garlic bread excluded. COLLISION RISK: dried spice-aisle 'minced garlic' shares the exact name; 'dried'/'dehydrated' catch the labeled ones but an unlabeled dried jar could still match.

label: Pickled Jalapenos (sliced)
note: Deliberately requires a jarred signal (pickled / sliced / nacho / diced / rings) so it does NOT steal FRESH whole jalapenos (existing produce item). Green chilies (candidate), banana peppers (candidate), and candied 'cowboy candy' jalapenos excluded. Integrator should add a 'pickled|nacho|sliced' exclude to the fresh-jalapeno rule to prevent the reverse hijack.

label: Green Olives (stuffed)
note: Green/manzanilla/spanish/pimiento-stuffed olives. Black/ripe olives (candidate) and kalamata routed to their own items; olive medleys/mixes and tapenade excluded. No 'oil' exclude needed: olive OIL cannot match any of these includes, and adding it would wrongly drop olives packed in oil.

label: Banana Peppers / Pepperoncini
note: Jarred banana pepper rings + pepperoncini (both spellings). Pickled jalapenos (candidate) and bell peppers excluded. MINOR COLLISION: fresh produce banana peppers share the name and there is no jarred-only keyword to gate on; rely on category/context.

label: Lime Juice (bottled)
note: Mirrors the existing lemon-juice rule. Requires 'lime ... juice', so fresh limes (produce) never match. Limeade/margarita mix/soda excluded. Bottled 'key lime juice' intentionally allowed; key lime PIE excluded via 'pie'.
